1218:

The estimate shall be made for the period or periods for which the person failed to make the report and shall be based upon any information which is in the board of commissioner's possession, or which may come into its possession pursuant to inspection or audit under section 78-70. Upon the basis of the estimate, the board of commissioners, or its designee, shall compute and determine the amount required to be paid, adding to the sum computed a penalty equal to 25 percent thereof. One or more determinations may be made for one or more periods. The tax amount determined to be paid shall be subject to any applicable interest or penalty provided for in this article.
(Ord. No. 03-1, § 2, 2-18-2003)

1227:
The occupation tax levied in this article is for revenue purposes. The occupation tax applies only to those businesses, practices and occupations which are covered by the provisions of O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-5—48-13-26. All other applicable businesses, practices and occupations are taxed by the local government pursuant to the pertinent general and/or local laws and ordinances.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1228:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Applicant means the natural person applying for the occupational tax benefit. For a sole proprietor the sole proprietor is the natural person application. For a partnership, corporation, limited liability company or other entity, the natural person applicant is an officer having authority to bind the entity.
Business means any person, partnership, corporation, limited liability company or other entity who engages in, causes to be engaged in, and/or is represented as being engaged in any occupation, practice of a profession, sale of any goods or services, commercial activity, or other activity with the object of financial gain, benefit or advantage, either directly or indirectly.
Dominant service or product means the type of service or product from which a business or practice providing multiple services or products derives the greatest amount of income.
Employee means an individual whose work is performed under the direction and supervision of the employer, and whose employer withholds FICA, federal income tax or state income tax from such individual's compensation, or whose employer issues to such individual, for purposes of documenting compensation, a form I.R.S. W-2, but not a form I.R.S. 1099.
First responder means peace officers certified under the Georgia Peace Officer Standards and Training Council as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 35-8-10 et seq., certified emergency medical technicians, paramedics, and cardiac technicians as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 31-11-52 et seq., and certified firefighters as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 25-4-1 et seq.
Location and office mean, and shall include, any structure or vehicle where a business, profession or occupation is conducted, but shall not include a temporary or construction work site which serves a single customer or project, or a vehicle used for sales or delivery by a business or practitioner of a profession or occupation which has a location or office.
Occupational tax means a tax levied on persons, partnerships, corporations or other entities for engaging in an occupation, profession or business which has been enacted by the county as a revenue-raising ordinance or resolution.
Practice, practitioner and practitioners of professions and occupations mean one who state law requires licensure regulating such profession or occupation. Such terms shall not include a practitioner who is an employee of a business if the business pays an occupation tax.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015; Ord. No. 16-04, § 1, 3-29-2016)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
1229:
For the calendar year 1995 and succeeding years thereafter, except those businesses and practitioners of professions and occupations excluded by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-16(a) each business and practitioner of professions and occupations with one or more locations or offices located within the county shall pay an occupation tax per fixed location as set out in this article.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1230:
(a) Those businesses, practitioners of professions and occupations with no location or office within the state shall pay an occupational tax, as set out in this article, if such business has one or more employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within the county for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or clients; or
(b) The number of employees of a business or practice, subject to this section, shall include only those employees engaged in substantial efforts within the state.
(c) Businesses and practitioners subject to this section shall be required to pay an occupation tax only to one local government in the state. Such payment will be made to the county only if the largest dollar volume of business is done or service is performed within the county.
(d) If a business or practitioner subject to this article provides the county development services division with proof of payment of a local business or occupation tax in another state which purports to tax the business' or practitioner's sales or services in the state, the business or practitioner shall be exempt from this county's occupational tax.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1231:
(a) The amount of occupation tax to be levied upon an individual business or practitioner shall be based upon the number of employees of the business or practitioner as follows:

(b) The number of employees shall be computed on a full-time position basis or a full-time position equivalent basis, provided that, for the purposes of such computation, an employee who works 40 hours or more weekly shall be considered a full-time employee, and that the average weekly hours of employees who work less than 40 hours weekly shall be added and such sum shall be divided by 40 to produce full-time equivalents.
(c) No business or practice shall be required to pay more than one occupation tax for each location of such business or practice. Each fixed location within the county where business or practice is conducted shall be considered a separate business for occupation tax purposes.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1232:
(a) Under the payment of the occupational taxes assessed in this article, it shall be the duty of the development services division to issue to each business an occupational tax certificate, provided that all information required has been furnished. The information required shall include the name and address of the business, a description of the type of business and the products and services being provided, the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code of the business, the number of employees, the applicant for the business and the applicant's relationship to the business, and any other information deemed necessary by the director. Provided further that the business or applicant is not disentitled to such under other provisions of this Code, or federal or state law. All businesses, other than a natural person as sole proprietor, are required to produce a certificate from the Georgia Secretary of State that such corporation is in good standing according to the records of his office.
(b) No tax certificate shall be issued unless the business and premises for which such application is made shall comply to all respects with the county zoning ordinance and with all other laws and ordinances applicable thereto.
(c) Those businesses, practitioners of professions and occupations with no location or office within the county shall be exempt from the occupational tax upon providing a completed occupational tax registration for businesses outside Columbia County and a paid occupational tax certificate from another jurisdiction within Georgia.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1233:
(a) Practitioners of professions and occupations listed in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c)(1)—(19) shall elect one of the following as their entire occupation tax:
(1) The occupation tax based on the number of employees, as set forth in section 78-140; or
(2) A fee per practitioner who is licensed to provide the service, as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk. A practitioner paying according to this subsection shall not be required to provide information to the county relating to the gross receipts of the business or practice. The per practitioner fee applies to each person in the business who qualifies as a practitioner under the state's regulatory guidelines and framework.
(b) The election between subsections (a)(1) and (a)(2) of this section shall be made on an annual basis, and must be submitted to the county development services division prior to January 1 of each calendar year.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1234:
(a) A business or practitioner with more than one type of service or product shall be classified according to such business' or practitioner's dominant service or product.
(b) The business or practice occupational tax certificate of each business or practice operated in the county shall identify the services or products provided by the business or practitioner. No business or practitioner shall provide or offer to provide any products or services without first having such product or service registered with the county's development services division, and shall have such noted on the business' or practitioner's occupational tax certificate which is required to be displayed.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1235:
(a) When more than one local government levies an occupation tax on a business or practitioner which has locations encompassed by the county and other local governments, and such governments use different criteria to establish the amount of occupation tax, the county shall base its tax on the number of employees who are employed within the county's geographical jurisdiction by such business or practitioner. In the case of an employee who works for the same business or practice in more than one municipal corporation or county, the county shall include such person as an employee in its occupation tax calculations if the employee works for the longest period of time within the calendar year within the county's geographic jurisdiction.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh.. A), 11-17-2015)
1236:
Occupational tax certificates shall not be transferrable. Transfer of ownership or change in location shall be treated as the termination of the business and the establishment of a new business and a new certificate shall be required.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1238:
Real estate brokers maintaining a principal or branch office within the county are subject to the occupation tax imposed by this article. The license, occupation or professional tax shall permit the broker and the broker's affiliated associate brokers and salespersons to engage in all of the brokerage activities set forth in O.C.G.A. § 43-40-1 without further licensing or taxing other than the state licenses identified pursuant to O.C.G.A. ch. 40, tit. 43. No additional license, occupation or professional tax shall be required of the broker's affiliated associate brokers or salespersons.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1239:
(a) The board of commissioners may, by subsequent ordinance or resolution, provide for an exemption or reduction in the occupation tax to one or more types of businesses or practitioners of occupations or professional as part of a plan for economic development or attracting, encouraging or maintaining selected types of businesses or practitioners of selected occupations or professions. Such exemptions or reductions in the occupation tax shall not be granted arbitrarily or capriciously, and the reasons for the granting of such exemption shall be set forth in the minutes of the meetings in which the board of commissioners makes such a determination.
(b) State and local authorities, as well as nonprofit organizations, are exempt from any occupation tax levy.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1240:
Each application for a new occupational tax under this article shall be accompanied by payment for the full amount of the tax. If the application is denied, the deposit representing the tax shall be refunded. All renewed occupation taxes, shall be due and payable annually within 30 days following January 1 of each year.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015; Ord. No. 25-05, § 1, 8-5-2025)
1241:
When any person commences business on or after July 1 in any calendar year, the occupation tax for the remaining portion of the year shall be 50 percent of the tax imposed for the entire year.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1242:
(a) Each business or practitioner shall exhibit and display all occupational tax certificates issued to them under this Code in a conspicuous place in their business establishment at which address the certificate was issued. Any transient or nonresident business or practitioner shall carry the occupational tax certificate either upon his person or in any vehicle or other conveyance which is used in the business and the person shall exhibit the same to any authorized enforcement or police officer.
(b) Each business or practitioner subject to any special or occupation tax under this article, who is also licensed by the state, shall post the state license in a conspicuous place in the licensee's place of business, and shall keep the license there at all times while the license remains valid.
(c) Any business or practitioner who is required to obtain health permits, bonds, certificates of qualification, certificates of competency or any other regulatory matter shall provide the county development services division with proof that such requirements has been fulfilled prior to providing or offering to provide services or products in the county.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1243:
The board of commissioners, through its designated representative, may inspect the books and records of any business or practitioner operating in the county for the purpose of verifying the information related to the calculation, assessment and collection of the occupation tax imposed by this article.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1245:
Where there is an apparent conflict in this article between specific and general provisions, it is the intention of this section that the specific shall control.
(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1246:
(a) Interest for all delinquent occupation taxes under this article shall accrue at a rate of 1.5 percent per month.
(b) Should any occupation tax imposed by this article remain due and unpaid for 90 days from the due date of such tax, the business or practitioner liable for the tax shall be subject to a penalty of ten percent of the tax due.
(c) Should any business or practitioner fail to renew its occupational tax certificate by July 1 following its expiration, the occupational tax certificate permitting the business will be automatically revoked.

(Ord. No. 15-29, § 1(Exh. A), 11-17-2015)
1247:
Any first responder shall be exempt from the payment of any occupational tax levied herein; provided however that this exemption shall only apply to the practice of such persons when they are working outside of their primary employment, as independent contractors on special assignments for which a license or certification is used or required.
(Ord. No. 16-04, § 2, 3-29-2016)
1250:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Department head means the employee, agent, contractor or elected official of the county charged with the responsibility of carrying out the duties set forth in this article.
Tax assessor means the employee in charge of the county tax assessor's office.
Tax commissioner means the county tax commissioner.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-1)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
1252:
Whenever a proposal to adopt or provide any of the improvements or services as set forth in section 78-192 has been filed with the board of commissioners, or the board of commissioners on their own motion have considered a proposal to furnish such improvement or to provide such utility, the board of commissioners shall cause the appropriate department head to make a preliminary survey and recommendation to the board of commissioners.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-3)
1253:
Whenever the board of commissioners shall determine from the preliminary survey that such project has merit and will serve a public need, and that the costs thereof shall be borne in whole or in part by the owners of the property affected, the board of commissioners shall set a time and place for a public hearing before the board of commissioners on such preliminary survey. Notice of such hearing shall be given to the owners of the property affected, by regular mail, if practicable, at least ten days in advance of such hearing, and by publication of such notice, one time, not less than ten days in advance of such hearing, in the newspaper in which notices of sheriff's sales for the county are published. Such notice shall generally describe the improvement or service to be constructed or furnished, the area affected and the manner in which the costs therefor shall be assessed or taxed against the owners of the affected property.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-4)
1254:
At the time and place fixed for a hearing as set forth in section 78-194, and after publication of the notice of such hearing, the board of commissioners shall proceed to hear the proposal, including objections thereto, if any, of any party at interest, and shall take such action rejecting such proposal, postponing such proposal until some future date, or approving the proposal, whichever action, in the judgment of the board of commissioners, will best promote the public interest.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-5)
1255:
If the proposal for service or improvement is accepted by the board of commissioners, and in the best judgment of the board of commissioners the costs of such work shall be assessed against the affected property owners, the board of commissioners shall pass a resolution authorizing the necessary work to be done in order to provide such improvement or service, and shall provide in such resolution the manner and method of assessing the costs therefor against the property owners affected, and designating the department head whose responsibility it is to carry out such proposals.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-6)
1256:
The department head charged by the resolution passed pursuant to section 78-196 shall, upon completion of the work or upon instituting the service, make a full report thereof to the board of commissioners, which report shall include the final costs of the project, and whether or not the costs, in whole or in part, to be assessed against the affected property owners is greater than or less than the amount anticipated in the preliminary survey.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-7)
1257:
Upon receipt of the report as set forth in section 78-197, the board of commissioners shall, if the cost is greater or less than the anticipated cost, pass a resolution providing for the amount to be assessed against the affected property owners.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-8)
1258:
The department head shall cause the affected property owner to be notified of the amount of the assessment as set forth in section 78-198, and shall collect the assessment in full in accordance with the terms and conditions of payment as set forth in the resolution. Failure to receive such notice shall not invalidate the assessment.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-9)
1259:
The costs of any improvement constructed pursuant to this article or resolution as set forth in this article shall be a lien upon the affected properties from the date of the completion of such improvement, and shall be enforceable in the same manner as executions for taxes are enforced, and shall have the same rank and character as liens for taxes.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-10)
1260:
Whenever the owner of any property shall fail to pay any assessment when due, the department head shall notify the clerk of the board of commissioners of the amount of the assessment in arrears, the name of the property owner and the affected property. The clerk shall issue an execution therefor, which execution shall be issued in the name of the board of commissioners, and shall be signed by the chairman of the board of commissioners. Such execution shall issue in rem against the property and in personam against the owner of such property, and in addition to the amount in arrears, shall include the sum as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk for the issuance of such execution. Subsequent costs shall be the same as those now allowed by law to the sheriff for the performance of similar services.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-11)
1261:
All executions issued against property and the owner of such property shall immediately be recorded on the general execution docket in the office of the clerk of the superior court, and shall be handed to the sheriff, and subsequent proceedings thereon shall be as provided by law for the enforcement of execution for taxes.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-12)
1262:
In the judgment of the board of commissioners, whenever services or improvements to be furnished under this article cannot be paid for in the manner and method provided in this article, the board of commissioners shall, by appropriate resolution, create a special tax district within the unincorporated areas of the county in which the services or improvements shall be furnished. Such resolution shall provide for the services or improvements to be furnished, the costs thereof, the area affected thereby and the amount to be assessed against each property owner in such district, and shall designate the department head who is charged with the responsibility of carrying out the improvements or services.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-13)
1263:
Upon completion of the improvements or institution of the services furnished pursuant to a resolution adopted under section 78-203, the department head shall notify the tax assessor and tax commissioner of the action taken, the district involved and the costs to be assessed against the property owners of such district.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-14)
1264:
The tax assessor's office shall compile a list of the property owners within the special tax district, and shall immediately furnish such list to the tax commissioner.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-15)
1265:
The tax commissioner shall, on the next succeeding tax bill, place on such tax bill the amount to be assessed against the property owners affected by such assessment, pursuant to the resolution for such work, which shall be collected in the same manner as other ad valorem taxes levied by the county.
(Code 1979, § 2-8-16)
1268:
As used in this article, the terms: "dealer;" "energy;" "local sales and use tax;" and "purchaser" shall have the same meanings as provided in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-110.
(Ord. No. 13-02, § 1, 4-2-2013)
1269:
In accordance with the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-110 et seq., there is imposed within the territorial limits of the special district created pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-111, an excise tax on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy when such sale, use, storage, or consumption would have constituted a taxable event for purposes of sales and use tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-1 et seq. but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2.
(Ord. No. 13-02, § 2, 4-2-2013)
1270:
(a) Such excise tax shall be levied and collected by the governing authority of Columbia County pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-112 and 48-13-114 and as provided in this section.
(b) Except as otherwise provided in this section, the rate of such excise tax shall be phased in over a four-year period as follows:
(1) For the period commencing January 1, 2013, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2013, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 25 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(2) For the period commencing January 1, 2014, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2014, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 50 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2;
(3) For the period commencing January 1, 2015, and concluding at the last moment of December 31, 2015, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 75 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2; and
(4) On or after January 1, 2016, such excise tax shall be at a rate equivalent to 100 percent of the total amount of local sales and use tax in effect in such special district that would be collected on the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy but for the exemption in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2.
(c) In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2(c)(4), if a project of regional significance under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3(92) is started in the special district, it shall not be subject to the phase-in period contained in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subsection (b) of this section, and the sale, use, storage, or consumption of energy in connection therewith shall be subject to the rate specified in paragraph (4) of subsection (b) of this section notwithstanding the January 1, 2016 limitation in that paragraph (4).
(d) (1) Following such initial imposition during the phase-in time period, on or after January 1, 2016, the rate of the excise tax levied and collected by the governing authority of Columbia County shall be directed by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-112(d). Such rate shall be controlled by the maximum amount of local sales and use tax in effect in the special district, but in no event more than two percent except in the case where the municipal option water and sewer tax is levied where that rate will be three percent within such municipality.
(2) In the event the total rate of local sales and use taxes in effect in the special district decreases from two percent to one percent, the rate of the excise tax under this article shall likewise be reduced at the same time such local sales and use tax rate reduction becomes effective.
(3) In the event the total rate of local sales and use taxes in effect in the special district increases from one percent to two percent, the rate of the excise tax under this article shall likewise be increased at the same time such local sales and use tax rate increase becomes effective.
(Ord. No. 13-02, § 3, 4-2-2013)
1272:
(a) The governing authority of Columbia County, or the collecting officer appointed under section 78-258 of this article, shall make diligent efforts to identify all energy providers and purchasers in the special district and to ascertain whether such a purchaser has completed a uniform exemption certificate provided from the website of the Georgia Department of Revenue seeking to qualify such purchaser for the exemption under O.C.G.A. § 48-8-3.2. Such certificate shall be utilized by such governing authority or collecting officer for the purpose of determining the applicability of the excise tax under this article.
(b) An energy provider shall be authorized to rely upon such uniform exemption certificates. An energy provider shall not be liable for failing to collect and remit the excise tax imposed pursuant to this article if the purchaser has failed to submit such uniform exemption certificate to the energy provider.
(Ord. No. 13-02, § 5, 4-2-2013)
1273:
(a) Due date of tax. The excise tax imposed pursuant to this article shall become effective upon the date of its adoption and shall be due and payable to the governing authority of Columbia County monthly on or before the twentieth day of every month and each respective month in which such taxes are collected, and payment shall be accompanied by a return for the preceding monthly period showing the gross sales and purchases arising from all sales and purchases taxable under this section during the preceding calendar month.
(b) Interest upon failure to pay tax. When any dealer fails to make any return or to pay the full amount of the tax required by an ordinance authorized by this article, there shall be imposed, in addition to other penalties provided by law, a penalty to be added to the tax in the amount of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for not more than 30 days and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional 30 days or fraction of 30 days during which the failure continues.
(c) Penalty for late payment. The penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00 in the aggregate, whichever is greater.
(d) Penalty for fraud or intent to invade. In the case of a false or fraudulent return or of a failure to file a return where willful intent exists to defraud the governing authority of any tax due under an ordinance authorized by this article, a penalty of 50 percent of the tax due shall be assessed.
(e) Mitigating factors. If the failure is due to providential cause, a dealer may demonstrate the applicability of such mitigation in the procedure set out in O.C.G.A. § 48-8-123 and if shown to the satisfaction of the Columbia County governing authority, the return may be accepted exclusive of penalties and interest.
(Ord. No. 13-02, § 6, 4-2-2013; Ord. No. 14-13, § 6, 11-4-2014; Ord. No. 18-05, § 1, 6-5-2018)
1274:
(a) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-114(b), the excise tax proceeds shall be allocated and distributed by the governing authority of Columbia County at the end of each calendar month. An amount equal to one percent of such proceeds collected by Columbia County shall be paid into the general fund of Columbia County to defray the costs of collection and administration.
(b) The remainder shall be distributed in accordance with the intergovernmental agreement as required under O.C.G.A. § 48-13-114(b) and (c). Within 30 days following the end of each calendar month, the remainder shall be distributed to the general fund of Columbia County and the general fund of each participating municipality in accordance with the applicable provisions of O.C.G.A. § 48-13-114(c)(1) or (2) as follows:

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this division, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Axle means a supporting shaft or member on which a wheel or pair of wheels revolves.
Boat means a craft designed to float on water.
Box truck means a self-powered, single unit vehicle with fully or partially enclosed cuboid space in which the cargo area is connected to the cabin by a single chassis or frame; refrigerated or unrefrigerated.
Bus means every motor vehicle designed for carrying more than 15 passengers.
Camper trailer means a trailer as defined in this section, which is pulled behind a motorized vehicle, and is used for recreational camping as a shelter or carrier for equipment.
Food truck means any motor vehicle, mobile vending unit, or trailer, equipped for storing, transporting, cooking, preparing, serving or selling food.
Home occupation vehicle means an allowed vehicle used as part of a licensed home occupation pursuant to section 90-142. Allowed vehicles include standard passenger vehicles, utility trailers, box trucks, food trucks, and trucks with service bodies or holding towing permits and specifically exclude tractor units or tractor trailers, dump trucks, concrete trucks, towing haulers, and other large vehicles.
Inoperative vehicle means a vehicle that cannot be driven upon public streets for any reasons including but not limited to being unlicensed, wrecked, abandoned, discarded, in a state of disrepair, partially dismantled, or incapable of being moved under its own power.
Large vehicle means flatbed trucks, dump trucks, concrete trucks, towing haulers, vehicles with service bodies or vehicles holding a towing permit or any large vehicle exceeding 10,000 pounds.
Limousine means any motor vehicle that meets the manufacturer's specifications for a luxury limousine with a designed seating capacity for no more than ten passengers and with a minimum of five seats located behind the operator of the vehicle, and which does not have a door at the rear of the vehicle designed to allow passenger entry or exit. Motor home means a motor vehicle built on a truck or bus chassis, and which is equipped to serve as self-contained living quarters for recreational travel.

Portable storage container means a self-storage container that is delivered to and retrieved from a home or business for long term off-site or on-site storage. Portable on demand storage or PODS are a familiar trade name for such containers. These containers are not on a chassis and do not have axles or wheels.

Trailer means a transport vehicle designed to be hauled by an automobile, truck or tractor unit.
Tractor unit means a heavy-duty towing engine that provides motive power for hauling a towed or trailered load, including but not limited to a semi-trailer.
Truck means a motorized vehicle designed and/or used for transporting loads.
Vehicle means a device, such as a motor vehicle or a piece of mechanized equipment, used for transporting passengers, goods, apparatuses or equipment.
Wrecker means any truck or other vehicle which is used to move or transport disabled, abandoned or other vehicles.

1365:
(a) Purpose.
(1) To protect the public potable water supply served by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services from the possibility of contamination or pollution by containment, within its customers internal distribution system, such contaminants or pollutants which could backflow or back-siphon into the public water system.
(2) To promote the elimination or control of existing cross-connections, actual or potential, between its customers in-plant potable water system, and non-potable systems.
(3) To provide for the maintenance of a continuing program of cross-connection control which will effectively prevent the contamination or pollution of all potable water systems by cross-connection.
(b) Authority.
(1) The Federal Safe Drinking Water Act of 1974, and the statutes of the State of Georgia Chapters 391-3-5.13 the water purveyor has the primary responsibility for preventing water from unapproved sources, or any other substances, from entering the public potable water system.
(2) Columbia County Water Utility, Rules and Regulations, adopted.
(c) Responsibility. The director of water and sewer services shall be responsible for the protection of the public potable water distribution system from contamination or pollution due to the backflow or backsiphonage of contaminants or pollutants through the water service connection. If, in the judgment of the director of the water and sewer services, an approved backflow device is required at the county's water service connection to any customer's promises, the director, or his delegated agent, shall give notice in writing to said customer to install an approved backflow prevention device at each service connection to his premises. The customer shall, within 90 days install such approved device, or devices, at his own expense, and failure or refusal, or inability on the part of the customer to install said device or devices within 90 days, shall constitute a ground for discontinuing water service to the premises until such device or devices have been properly installed. Backflow assemblies are to be installed by a licensed plumber, licensed fire protection system installer, and/or licensed underground utility contractor on all new installations only. Backflow assemblies that are retrofits and upgrades must be installed by a licensed plumber. All repairs are to be made by a licensed master plumber or someone certified by the State of Georgia in backflow device repair. The device requires an initial test within five days of installation and then annually tested by a certified backflow tester to assure that it is functioning correctly and forwarded to the compliance office.
(d) Definitions.
Approved. Accepted by the director of the water and sewer services as meeting an applicable specification stated or cited in this regulation, or as suitable for the proposed use.
Auxiliary water supply. Any water supply, on or available, to the premises other than the purveyor's approved public potable water supply.
Backflow. The flow of water or other liquids, mixtures or substances, under positive or reduced pressure in the distribution pipes of a potable water supply from any source other than its intended source.
Backflow preventer. A device or means designed to prevent backflow or backsiphonage. Most commonly categorized as air gap, reduced pressure principle device, double check valve assembly, pressure vacuum breaker, atmospheric vacuum breaker, hose bibb vacuum breaker, residential dual check, double check with intermediate atmospheric vent, and barometric loop.
(1) Air gap. A physical separation sufficient to prevent backflow between the free-flowing discharge end of the potable water system and any other system. Physically defined as a distance equal to twice the diameter of the supply side pipe diameter but never less than one inch.
(2) Atmospheric vacuum breaker. A device which prevents backsiphonage by creating an atmospheric vent when there is either a negative pressure or sub-atmospheric pressure in a water system.
(3) Double check valve assembly. An assembly of two independently operating spring loaded check valves with tightly closing shut off valves on each side of the check valves, plus properly located test cocks for the testing of each check valve.
(4) Hose bibb vacuum breaker. A device which is permanently attached to a hose bibb and which acts as an atmospheric vacuum breaker.
(5) Pressure vacuum breaker. A device containing one or two independently operated spring loaded check valves and an independently operated spring loaded air inlet valve located on the discharge side of the check or checks. Device includes tightly closing shut-off valves on each side of the check valves and properly located test cocks for the testing of the check valve(s).
(6) Reduced pressure principle backflow preventer. An assembly consisting of two independently operating approved check valves with an automatically operating differential relief valve located between the two check valves, tightly closing shut-off valves on each side of the check valves plus properly located test cocks for the testing of the check valves and the relief valve.
(7) Residential dual check. An assembly of two spring loaded, independently operating check valves without tightly closing shut-off valves and test cocks. Generally employed immediately downstream of the water meter to act as a containment device.
Backpressure. A condition in which the owners system pressure is greater than the suppliers system pressure.
Backsiphonage. The flow of water or other liquids, mixtures or substances into the distribution pipes of a potable water supply system from any source other than its intended source caused by the sudden reduction of pressure in the potable water supply system.
Commissioners. Columbia County Board of Commissioners.
Containment. A method of backflow prevention which requires a backflow prevention preventer at the water service entrance.
Contaminant. A substance that will impair the quality of the water to a degree that it creates a serious health hazard to the public leading to poisoning or the spread of disease.
Cross-connection. Any actual or potential connection between the public water supply and a source of contamination or pollution.
Department. Columbia County Water and Sewer Services.
Director of water and sewer services. The director, or his delegated representative in charge of the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services, is invested with the authority and responsibility for the implementation of a cross-connection control program and for the enforcement of the provisions of the chapter.
DNR. Department of Natural Resource.
EPD. Environmental Protection Division.
Fixture isolation. A method of backflow prevention in which a backflow preventer is located to correct a cross-connection at an in-plant location rather than at a water service entrance.
Owner. Any person, who has legal title to, or license to operate or habitat in, a property upon which a cross-connection inspection is to be made or upon which a cross-connection is present.
Person. Any individual, partnership, company, public or private corporation, political subdivision or agency of the state department, agency or instrumentality or the United States or any other legal entity.
Permit. A document issued by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services Compliance Office which allows the use of a backflow preventer.
Pollutant. A foreign substance, that if permitted to get into the public water system, will degrade its quality so as to constitute a moderate hazard, or impair the usefulness or quality of the water to a degree which does not create an actual hazard to the public health but which does adversely and unreasonably effect such water for domestic use.
Water service entrance. That point in the owners water system beyond the sanitary control of the district; generally considered to be the outlet end of the water meter and always before any unprotected branch.
(e) Administration.
(1) The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will operate a cross-connection control program, to include the keeping of necessary records, which fulfills the requirements of the commission's cross-connection regulations and is approved by the commission.
(2) The owner shall allow his property to be inspected for possible cross-connections and shall follow the provisions of the department's program and the commission's regulations if a cross-connection is permitted.
(3) If the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services requires that the public supply be protected by containment, the owner shall be responsible for water quality beyond the outlet end of the containment device and should utilize fixture outlet protection for that purpose.
He may utilize public health officials, or personnel from the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services, or their delegated representatives, to assist him in the survey of his facilities and to assist him in the selection of proper fixture outlet devices, and the proper installation of these devices.
(f) Requirements.
(1) Columbia County Water Utility.
a. On new installations, the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will provide on-site evaluation and/or inspection of plans in order to determine the type of backflow preventer, if any, that will be required, will issue permit, and perform inspection and testing. In any case, a minimum of a double check valve with a wye strainer will be required in any new commercial construction and a minimum of a dual check on any residential.
b. For premises existing prior to the start of this program, the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will perform evaluations and inspections of plans and/or premises and inform the owner by letter of any corrective action deemed necessary, the method of achieving the correction, and the time allowed for the correction to be made. Ordinarily, 90 days will be allowed, however, this time period may be shortened depending upon the degree of hazard involved and the history of the device(s) in question.
c. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will not allow any cross-connection to remain unless it is protected by an approved backflow preventer for which a permit has been issued and which will be regularly tested to insure satisfactory operation.
d. If the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services determines at any time that a serious threat to the public health exists, the water service will be terminated immediately.
e. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services shall have on file, a list of private contractors who are certified backflow device testers. All charges for these tests will be paid by the owner of the building or property.
f. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services requires all reduced pressure principle devices and double check valve backflow preventers include the installation of strainers located immediately upstream of the backflow device. The installation of strainers will preclude the fouling of backflow devices due to both foreseen and unforeseen circumstances occurring to the water supply system such as water main repairs, water main breaks, fires, periodic cleaning, and flushing of mains, etc. These occurrences may "stir up" debris within the water main that will cause fouling of backflow devices installed without the benefit of strainers.
(2) Owner.
a. The owner shall be responsible for the elimination or protection of all cross-connections on his premises.
b. The owner, after having been informed by a letter from the department, shall at his expense, install, maintain, and test, or have tested, any and all backflow preventers on his premises.
c. The owner shall correct any malfunction of the backflow preventer which is revealed by periodic testing.
d. The owner shall inform the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services of any proposed or modified cross-connections and also any existing cross-connections of which the owner is aware but has not been found by the department.
e. The owner shall not install a bypass around any backflow preventer unless there is a backflow preventer of the same type on the bypass. Owners who cannot shut down operation for testing of the device(s) must supply additional devices necessary to allow testing to take place.
f. The owner shall install backflow preventers in a manner approved by the Columbia County Water Utility.
g. The owner shall install only backflow preventers approved by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services or the EPD.
h. Any owner having a private well or other private water source, must have a permit if the well or source is cross-connected to the Columbia County Water Utility's system. Permission to cross-connect may be denied by the Columbia County Water Utility. The owner may be required to install a backflow preventer at the service entrance if a private water source is maintained, even if it is not cross-connected to the Columbia County Water Utility's system.
i. In the event the owner installs plumbing to provide potable water for domestic purposes which is on the Columbia County Water Utility's side of the backflow preventer, such plumbing must have its own backflow preventer installed.
j. The owner shall be responsible for the payment of all fees for permits, annual or semi-annual device testing, retesting in the case that the device fails to operate correctly, and second re-inspections for non-compliance with the Columbia County Water Utility.
(g) Degree of hazard. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services recognizes the threat to the public water system arising from cross-connections. All threats will be classified by degree of hazard and will require the installation of approved reduced pressure principle backflow prevention devices or double check valves.
(h) Permits. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services shall not permit a cross-connection within the public water supply system unless it is considered necessary and that it cannot be eliminated.
(1) Cross-connection permits that are required for each backflow prevention device are obtained from the Columbia County Water Utility.
(2) Permits shall be renewed annually and are non-transferable. Permits are subject to revocation and become immediately revoked if the owner should so change the type of cross-connection or degree of hazard associated with the service.
(3) An initial inspection permit is required on new residential dual check backflow preventer.
(i) Existing in-use backflow prevention devices. Any existing backflow preventer shall be allowed by the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services to continue in service unless the degree of hazard is such as to supersede the effectiveness of the present backflow preventer, or result in an unreasonable risk to the public health. Where the degree of hazard has increased, an in the case of a residential installation converting to a business establishment, any existing backflow preventer must be upgraded to a reduced pressure principle device, or a reduced pressure principle device must be installed in the event that no backflow device was present.
(j) Periodic testing.
(1) All backflow devices shall be tested and inspected at least annually.
(2) Testing must be performed by licensed backflow tester approved by the State of Georgia.
(3) Any backflow preventer which fails during a periodic test will be repaired or replaced at owner's expense. When repairs are necessary, upon completion of the repair the device will be retested at owner's expense to insure correct operation. High hazard situations will not be allowed to continue unprotected if the backflow preventer fails the test and cannot be repaired immediately. In other situations, a compliance date of not more than 30 days after the test date will be established. The owner is responsible for spare parts, repair tools, or a replacement device. Parallel installation of two devices is an effective means of the owner insuring that uninterrupted water service during testing or repair of devices and is strongly recommended when the owner desires such continuity. Backflow prevention devices will be tested more frequently than specified in subsection (1), above, in cases where there is a history of test failures and the Columbia County Water and Sewer Services feels that due to the degree of hazard involved, additional testing is warranted. Cost of the additional tests will be borne by the owner.
(k) Records and reports.
(1) Records. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will initiate and maintain the following:
a. Master files on customer cross-connection tests and/or inspections.
b. Master files on cross-connection permits.
c. Copies of permits and permit applications.
d. Copies of lists and summaries supplied to the EPD.
(2) Reports. The Columbia County Water and Sewer Services will submit the following to the EPD.
a. Initial listing of low hazard cross-connections to the state.
b. Initial listing of high hazard cross-connections to the state.
c. Annual update lists of subsection a. and b. above.
d. Annual summary of cross-connection inspections to the state.
(l) Fees and charges.
(1) The Columbia County Board of Commissioners has established fees under this article or charges for the following services or permits:
a. Initial inspection fees.
b. Annual inspection fees.
c. Water trucks and tank permit fee.
d. Citations and violations.
(2) A list of the fees is on file at the clerk of court and the Columbia County Water Utility.
(3) The fees for such inspections shall be issued for a period of one year. All permits will expire at 12:00 midnight on the date specified on the permit as determined by the Columbia County Water Utility.
(4) Citations and violations for lack of compliance will be determined and applied to the inspection fee.
(m) Water trucks and tanks inspection and permit fee.
(1) Water trucks and tanks shall be inspected annually by Columbia County Water and Sewer Services and be issued a permit number and decal that shall be placed on the tank.
(2) Water trucks and tanks shall have a RFZ backflow assembly or an air gap two times the diameter of the fill pipe and not less than one inch.
(3) The fees for such inspections shall be issued for a period of one year. All permits will expire at 12:00 midnight on the date specified on the permit as determined by the Columbia County Water Utility.
(4) Citations for lack of compliance will be determined.
(5) The Columbia County Board of Commissioners has established fees under this article or charges for the following services or permits:
a. Potable water trucks inspection.
b. Non-potable water trucks inspection.
c. Mobile tanks inspection.
(6) A list of the fees is on file at the clerk of commission and the business office of Columbia County Water Utility.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Act means the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, also known as the Clean Water Act, as amended, 33 USC § 1251 et seq.
Authorized representative of user means:
(1) If the user is a corporation, the:
a. President, secretary, treasurer or vice-president of the corporation in charge of a principal business function, or any other person who performs similar policy or decision-making functions for the corporation; or
b. Manager of one or more manufacturing, production or operation facilities employing more than 250 persons, or having gross annual sales or expenditures exceeding $25,000,000.00, if authority to sign documents has been assigned or delegated to the manager in accordance with corporate procedures.
(2) A general partner or proprietor, respectively, if the user is a partnership or sole proprietor.
(3) If the user is a federal, state or local governmental facility, a director or the highest official appointed or designated to oversee the operation and performance of the activities of the government facility or his designee.

a. The authorization is in writing by such individual, and the authorization specifies an individual or position responsible for the overall operation of the facility from which the discharge originates; or
b. Has overall responsibility for environmental matters for the company; and
c. The written authorization is submitted to the director.
(5) If an authorization under subsection (4) of this definition is no longer accurate, a new authorization satisfying the requirements of subsection (4) of this definition must be submitted to the director prior to or together with any reports to be signed by an authorized representative.
Biochemical oxygen demand and BOD mean the quantity of oxygen utilized in the biochemical oxidation of organic matter under standard laboratory procedures for five days at 20 degrees Celsius, usually expressed as a concentration (e.g., mg/l).
Building sewer means the extension from a building drain to the public sewer or other place of disposal, also known as house connection or service connection.
Categorical pretreatment standard and categorical standard mean any regulation containing pollutant discharge limits promulgated by the EPA in accordance with section 307(b) and (c) of the Act (33 USC § 1317) which applies to a specific category of users, and which appear in 40 CFR 405—471, chapter I, subchapter N.
Commission and county commission mean the board of commissioners of the county, which has jurisdiction over the maintenance and operations of the water and sanitary sewer system within the county.
Director means the director of the county water utility services division.
Environmental protection division and EPD mean the state department of natural resources division, environmental protection division.
Existing source means any source of discharge, the construction or operation of which commenced prior to the publication by the EPA of the proposed categorical pretreatment standards, which will be applicable to such source if the standard is promulgated in accordance with section 307 of the Act.
Filtration/inflow means groundwater and surface water which leaks into the sewers through cracked pipes, joints, manholes or other openings.
Floatable oil means oil, fat or grease in a physical state such that it will separate by gravity from wastewater by treatment in an approved pretreatment facility. Wastewater shall be considered free of floatable oil if it is properly pretreated in an approved grease trap, and the wastewater does not interfere with the POTW.
Food service establishment means any restaurant, eatery, food caterer, cafeteria, hospital, school, institution, motel, hotel, prison, business or similar place, other than dwelling units, where food is prepared for sale, delivery or consumption.
Garbage means the animal and vegetable waste resulting from the handling, preparation, cooking and serving of food.
Grab sample means a sample which is taken from a waste stream without regard to the flow in the waste stream. The sample may be taken over a period of time not to exceed 15 minutes.
Grease trap means a device primarily used in the food service industry for removal of oil, grease and food solids from a process prior to discharge into the POTW.
Indirect discharge means the introduction of pollutants into the POTW from any nondomestic source regulated under section 307(b), (c) or (d) of the Act.
Industrial user means a nonresidential user identified in Division A, B, C, D, E or I of the standard industrial classification. This term shall also include any significant industrial user.
Industrial waste means the wastewater from industrial processes as distinct from domestic or sanitary wastes.
Interference means a discharge, which alone or in conjunction with discharges from other sources, which inhibits or disrupts the POTW or public sewer, its treatment processes or operations, or its sludge processes, use or disposal, and therefore, is a cause of a violation of the county's NPDES permit or of the prevention of sewerage sludge use or disposal in compliance with the following statutory/regulatory provisions or permits issued under the NPDES permit, or any more stringent state or local regulations: Section 405 of the act; the SWDA; and state regulations contained in any state sludge management plan prepared pursuant to Subtitle D of the SWDA; the Clean Air Act, 42 USC § 7401 et seq.; the Toxic Substances Control Act, 15 USC § 2601 et seq.; and the Marine Protection, Research and Sanctuaries Act, 16 USC § 1361 et seq.
Mass emission rate means the weight of material discharged to the public sewer during a given time interval. Unless otherwise specified in this article, the mass emission rate shall mean pounds per day (lbs./d) of a particular constituent or combination of constituents.
Medical waste means isolation wastes, infectious agents, human blood and blood products, pathological wastes, sharps, body parts, contaminated bedding, surgical wastes, potentially contaminated laboratory wastes and dialysis wastes.
May is permissive.
National categorical pretreatment standard and pretreatment standard mean a regulation containing pollutant discharge limits applicable to a specific category of industrial users, promulgated by the EPA in accordance with section 307(b) and (c) of the Act (33 USC § 1317). This term includes prohibited discharge limits established pursuant to 40 CFR 403.5.
National Pollution Discharge Elimination System permit and NPDES permit mean a permit issued pursuant to section 402 of the Act (33 USC § 1342).
Natural outlet means a discharge into a watercourse, pond, ditch, lake or other body of surface water or groundwater.
New source means:
(1) A building, structure, facility or installation from which there is a discharge of pollutants, the construction of which commenced after the publication of proposed pretreatment standards under section 307(c) of the Act, which will be applicable to such source if such standards are thereafter promulgated in accordance with such section, provided that the:
a. Building, structure, facility or installation is constructed at a site at which no other source is located;
b. Building, structure, facility or installation totally replaces the process or production equipment that causes the discharge of pollutants at an existing source; or
c. Production or wastewater generating processes of the building, structure, facility or installation are substantially independent of an existing source at the same site.
In determining whether these are substantially independent, factors such as the extent to which the new facility is integrated with the existing plant and the extent to which the new facility is engaged in the same general type of activity as the existing source should be considered.
(2) Construction on a site at which an existing source is located results in a modification rather than a new source if the construction does not create a new building, structure, facility or installation meeting the criteria of subsection (1)b. or (1)c. of this definition, but otherwise alters, replaces or adds to existing process or production equipment.
(3) Construction of a new source has commenced if the owner or operator has:
a. Begun, or caused to begin, as part of a continuous on-site construction program:
1. Any placement, assembly or installation of facilities or equipment; or
2. Significant site preparation work including clearing, excavation or removal of existing buildings, structures or facilities which is necessary for the placement, assembly or installation of new source facilities or equipment; or
b. Entered into a binding contractual obligation for the purchase of facilities or equipment which are intended to be used in its operation within a reasonable time. Options to purchase or contracts which can be terminated or modified without substantial loss, and contracts for feasibility, engineering and design studies do not constitute a contractual obligation under this definition.
Noncontact cooling water means water used for cooling which does not come into direct contact with any raw material, intermediate product, waste product or finished product.
Pass through means a discharge which exits the POTW into waters of the United States in quantities or concentrations which, alone or in conjunction with discharges from other sources, is a cause of violation of any requirement of the county's NPDES permit, including an increase in the magnitude or duration of a violation.
pH means a measure of the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, expressed in standard units (grams per liter of solution).
Pollutant means impurities in water that include, but are not limited to, dredged spoil, solid waste, incinerator residue, filter backwash, sewage, garbage, sewerage sludge, munitions, medical wastes, chemical wastes, biological materials, radioactive materials, heat, wrecked or discarded equipment, rock, sand, cellar dirt, municipal, agricultural and industrial wastes, and certain characteristics of wastewater (e.g., when pH, temperature, TSS, turbidity, color, BOD, COD, toxicity or odor cause adverse effects in the POTW).
Pollution means the manmade or man-induced alteration of the chemical, physical, biological or radiological integrity of water.
Pretreatment means the reduction of the amount of pollutants, the elimination of pollutants or the alteration of the nature of pollutant properties in wastewater prior to or in lieu of introducing such pollutants into the POTW. This reduction or alteration can be obtained by physical, chemical or biological processes; by process changes; or by other means, except by diluting the concentration of the pollutants unless expressly allowed by an applicable pretreatment standard or requirement.
Pretreatment requirement means any substantive or procedural requirement related to pretreatment imposed on a user, other than a national pretreatment standard.
Pretreatment standards mean prohibited discharge standards, categorical pretreatment standards and local limits.
Prohibited discharge standards or discharges mean absolute prohibitions against the discharge of certain substances which are set forth in section 86-133.
Publicly owned treatment works and POTW mean treatment works as defined by section 212 of the Act (33 USC § 1292), which are owned by the county. This definition includes any devices or systems used in collection, storage, treatment, recycling and reclamation of sewage or industrial waste of a liquid nature, and any conveyances which convey wastewater to a treatment plant.
Representative sample means a portion of wastewater that is small enough in volume to be transported conveniently while accurately displaying the characteristics of the wastewater being sampled.
Residential user means a premises used for human residency or habitation.
Sanitary wastewater means wastewater discharged into the POTW from the sanitary conveniences of dwellings, office buildings, industrial plants or institutions.
Septic tank means a sewage disposal tank in which a continuous flow of waste material is decomposed by anaerobic bacteria.
Sewage means human excrement and gray water (household showers, dish washing operations, etc.).
Significant industrial user means a user which:
(1) a. Is subject to categorical pretreatment standards;
b. Has in its waste a toxic pollutant in toxic amounts as defined in standards issued under section 307(a) of the Act;
c. Discharges an average of 25,000 gpd or more of process wastewater to the POTW, excluding sanitary, noncontact cooling water, sanitary and boiler blow down wastewater;
d. Contributes a process waste stream which makes up five percent or more of the average dry weather hydraulic or organic capacity of the POTW treatment plant; or
e. Is designated as such by the county on the basis that it has a reasonable potential or in combination with other contributing industries for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement.
(2) Upon finding that a user meeting the criteria in subsections (1)b. and c. of this definition has no reasonable potential for adversely affecting the POTW's operation or for violating any pretreatment standard or requirement, the county may, at any time, on its own initiative or in response to a petition received from a user and in accordance with procedures set forth in 40 CFR 403.8(f)(6), determine that such user should not be considered a significant industrial user.
Significant noncompliance means:
(1) Chronic violations of wastewater discharge limits, which are defined as those in which 66 percent or more of wastewater measurements taken during a six-month period exceed the daily maximum limit or average limit for the same pollutant parameter by any amount;
(2) Technical review criteria (TRC) violations, which are defined as those in which 33 percent or more of wastewater measurements taken for each pollutant parameter during a six-month period equals or exceeds the product of the daily maximum limit or the average limit multiplied by the applicable criteria (1.4 for BOD, TSS, fats, oils and grease, and 1.2 for all other pollutants except pH);
(3) Any other discharge violation that the director believes has caused, alone or in combination with other discharges, interference or pass through, including endangering the health of POTW personnel or the general public;
(4) Any discharge of pollutants that has caused imminent endangerment to the public or to the environment, or has resulted in the director's exercise of emergency authority to halt or prevent such a discharge;
(5) Failure to meet, within 90 days of the scheduled date, a compliance schedule milestone contained in a wastewater discharge permit or enforcement order for starting construction, completing construction or attaining final compliance;
(6) Failure to provide, within 30 days after the due date, any required reports, including baseline monitoring reports, reports on compliance with categorical pretreatment standard deadlines, periodic self-monitoring reports and reports on compliance with compliance schedules;
(7) Failure to accurately report noncompliance; or
(8) Any other violation which the director determines will adversely affect the operation or implementation of the local pretreatment program.
Slug means a discharge at a flow rate or concentration which could cause a violation of the prohibited discharge standards set forth in section 86-133.
Standard industrial classification (SIC) means a classification pursuant to the Standard Industrial Classification Manual issued by the Executive Office of the President, Office of Management and Budget.
Stormwater means a flow that occurs during or following any form of natural precipitation and results from such precipitation, including snow-melt.
Suspended solids mean the total suspended matter that floats on the surface of or is suspended in water, wastewater or other liquids, and which is removable by laboratory filtering.
Shall is mandatory.
Toxic pollutant means a pollutant or combination of pollutants listed as toxic in regulations promulgated by the administrator of the EPA under the provisions of the Act.
Upset means the disturbance of the normal function of an industry's pretreatment facility caused by an unanticipated abnormal event which resulted in the industry's wastewater discharge not being compliant with the industry's wastewater discharge permit limitations.
User means a person who contributes, causes or permits the contribution of wastewater into the county's POTW.
Waste hauler means a person that transports waste by a means other than direct connection to the POTW.
Waste stream formula means the waste stream formula set forth in 40 CFR 403.6(e).
Wastewater means the spent water of a community. From the standpoint of source, wastewater may be a combination of liquid and water-carried wastes from residences, commercial buildings, industrial plants and institutions, together with any groundwater, surface water and stormwater that may be present.

(d) When BOD, suspended solids or grease concentrations in the user's wastewater discharge are in excess of the range of concentration in normal strength wastewater, a surcharge shall be added to the base charge as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk. 1393:
(a) Where the public sewer system is not available, the building sewer shall be connected to a private septic tank system complying with the provisions of this article.
(b) Before commencement of construction of a private septic tank system, the owner shall first obtain a written permit signed by the county board of health. The application for such permit shall be made on a form furnished by the board of health, which the applicant shall supplement by any plans, specifications and other information deemed necessary by the county engineer or board of health.
(c) A permit for a private septic tank system shall not become effective until the installation of the private septic tank system is completed to the satisfaction of the board of health. The board of health shall be allowed to inspect the work at any stage of construction and the applicant for the permit shall notify the board of health when the work is ready for final inspection and before any underground portions of the private septic tank system are covered, excluding the building sewer to the private septic tank system.
(d) The type, capacities, location and layout of a private septic tank system shall comply with all recommendations of the state department of public health, and shall comply with the provisions of this article. No private septic tank or cesspool shall be permitted to discharge to any natural outlet.
(e) At the time that a public sewer system becomes available to a property served by a private septic tank system, as provided in subsection 86-124(c), a notification to connect to the public sewer system may be made by the director. A direct connection shall be made to the public sewer system in compliance with this article within 30 days of such notification. If connection is made to the POTW, the private septic tanks shall be abandoned and filled with suitable material.
(Code 1979, § 2-7-36)
1394:
In checking a private septic tank system in the county, the operation and maintenance of on-site sewage disposal systems shall be as set forth in chapter 290-5-26 of the rules and regulations of the department of human resources public health, as adopted by the state department of human resources, filed January 23, 1998, effective February 20, 1998, and such rules and regulations as may be amended by the department of human resources, which are incorporated into and made a part of this Code subject to the enforcement provisions in this article.
(Code 1979, § 2-7-37)
1395:
The county board of health shall have the authority to adopt such further regulations as it determines to be necessary and proper for on-site sewage management systems, including, but not limited to, private septic tank systems, to the full extent permitted by state law.
(Code 1979, § 2-7-38)
1396:
The county board of health or its authorized agent shall be authorized to enforce sections 86-127—86-129 and to issue citations for violations of the provisions of such sections, and shall be authorized to enter upon any premises or properties located within the county at any reasonable time as may be necessary for inspection and enforcement. Any person who shall violate the provisions of sections 86-127—86-129 shall, upon conviction, be subject to punishment as set forth in section 86-178.
(Code 1979, § 2-7-39)
1397:
(a) Septic tank waste may be introduced into the POTW only at locations designated by the director, and at such times as are established by the director. The director may require septic tank waste haulers to obtain wastewater discharge permits.
(b) A waste hauler shall:
(1) Discharge septic tank waste loads at times and locations specifically designated by the director.
(2) Be limited to discharging only domestic wastes.
(3) Purchase a waste hauler discharge ticket from the county water and sewer services division using a form and paying a price as set forth in the schedule of fees and charges on file in the office of the county clerk which shall be determined by the board of commissioners. The ticket must be presented to the operator prior to any discharge.
(4) Provide prior notice to the director of the intent to discharge, and the actual discharge must be performed under the supervision of plant personnel.
(5) Be prohibited from discharging any waste which would violate federal, state or local regulations.
(6) If required by the director, provide a completed waste manifest form which shall contain information regarding the waste and the signature of each waste generator. The hauler shall also sign the form indicating that he has accepted no wastes other than those listed on such form.
(7) If required by the director, provide a waste analysis of any load prior to discharge. The director may collect samples of each hauled load to ensure compliance with applicable standards.
(8) Carry liability insurance in such amounts and in the form as determined by the board of commissioners, and provide satisfactory evidence of such insurance coverage to the county. Such insurance shall afford compensation for taking corrective action, bodily injury and property damage to third persons caused by hauler negligence and/or accidents.
(c) The director shall require haulers of industrial waste to obtain wastewater discharge permits. The director may require generators of hauled industrial waste to obtain wastewater discharge permits. The director may also prohibit the disposal of hauled industrial waste. The discharge of hauled industrial waste is subject to all other requirements set forth in this article.
(Code 1979, § 2-7-40)
